facts.fact: 一周后她在 2nd Ave 撞见 Silverman 出工：5W 门牌旧名被涂白、新写上 Hutchinson/Barrymore，门上新贴 No Loitering 告示——违规者将被起诉（章题出处）。
facts.anchor: There was also a No Loitering note freshly taped to the door. Violators Will Be Prosecuted.

facts.fact: 她在古着店 Combat 打工却恨古着：恨衣物里的霉味、恨「有人穿着它死掉」的确定感——无法对穿过衣服的前人生活不好奇。
facts.anchor: I hate the must that settles into the clothes, the certainty that someone died with that shirt thrown over the chair.

facts.fact: 老板 Cynthia（前嬉皮、永恒的机会主义者、水晶爱好者）飘着音调说：衣服值多少钱就是多少钱，价值随时间变——她暗指某本好书的相反论点。
facts.anchor: “The coat costs what it’s worth,” Cynthia said in an ethereal tone.

facts.fact: 朋友圈职业生态：除了 Julie（律师）与 Claude（护士）人人辗转端盘子、调酒、性工作、搬运、开出租、送毒；Mark 在四大道旧书店打工还接受老男人付费口交。
facts.anchor: Everyone I knew, save Julie the lawyer and Claude the nurse, cycled through waiting tables and bartending and hooking and stripping and box schlepping and art schlepping and driving cabs and riding bikes and delivering drugs.

facts.fact: 谁看上 Mark 他就有钱，还会当天把横财分给公园里随口说手头紧的熟人；房租从没均摊、从未准时。
facts.anchor: Mark occasionally had a lot of it if someone took a shine to him, and he’d share his loot with whomever he ran into in the park that day and happened to mention they were tight.

facts.fact: 试衣间外的闲话：一个女孩告诉男友自己有 AIDS 就被他勒死——停顿一秒后接「这裙子显得我好胖」；恐怖与虚荣共用一句话。
facts.anchor: I read that she was making it with the guy and told him she had AIDS and he flew into a rage and strangled her.

facts.fact: 新住户 Diane：搬进来自从听到砰砰声、Carolyn 总觉得夜里房间有「东西」；父母朋友的女儿也请过这公司、问题消失了——父母付钱，「他们想让我有安全感；我是学生」，仿佛学生就豁免于世界。
facts.anchor: And Carolyn kept feeling like there was something in her room at night, so.

facts.fact: 她追问 Carolyn：夜里真有人进过你房间？——那是个真问题，她不想让它被误认成超自然；Carolyn 含混答「某个东西」。
facts.anchor: “Someone was in your room at night?” That would be an actual problem I didn’t want her to mistake for supernatural.

facts.fact: Diane 买裙子：原价 15 美元被她报价 39.95（现金 35）；Carolyn 嫌贵，Diane 说「这是古着（It's vintage）」。
facts.anchor: As Diane pulled out two twenties, Carolyn said, “That’s a little much, isn’t it?”

facts.fact: 两人走后她把 20 美元放进收银机、其余进自己口袋当提成——想着偶尔干一次，就不用总缠着 Cynthia 要求加薪。
facts.anchor: After they left, I put twenty bucks in the cash register and pocketed the rest as commission.
